This algorithm performs one finite-budget LM trial update. Inputs are $x\in U$, a $C^1$ residual function $r:U\to\mathbb R^m$ on open $U$ with $m,n\ge1$ and $J=Dr$, the exact values $r(x)$ and $J(x)$, a fixed nonsingular $D\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, an arithmetic mode (exact or computed), a floor $\lambda_{\min}>0$, current damping $\lambda\ge\lambda_{\min}$, factors $\gamma>1$, $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$, a trust radius $\Delta>0$, and an attempt cap $N\ge1$. In computed mode the input values are finite stored numbers treated as the exact data for this update; only arithmetic performed below is rounded. A computed run may include a certificate that the exact scalar product $J(x)^Tr(x)$ is zero. Put $\phi(x)=\|r(x)\|_2^2/2$ and $m_0(p)=\|r(x)+J(x)p\|_2^2/2$. In exact mode the step is the unique minimizer of $$\tfrac12\|r(x)+J(x)p\|_2^2+\tfrac\lambda2\|Dp\|_2^2,$$ which is equivalent to solving $$(J(x)^TJ(x)+\lambda D^TD)p=-J(x)^Tr(x).$$ In computed mode the returned vector is only a candidate for this same subproblem; no exact minimizer claim is made.

Let $F$ be a complete ordered field ([[def-complete-ordered-field]]). Then every $a \in F$ with $a \ge 0$ has a **unique** $s \in F$ with $s \ge 0$ and $s^2 = a$; we write $s = \sqrt{a}$. Consequently the positive elements of $F$ are exactly the nonzero squares: $x > 0$ if and only if $x = y^2$ for some $y \neq 0$.

1. In exact arithmetic, if $J(x)^Tr(x)=0$, return stationary before calling the linear solver. In a computed run, evaluate $J(x)^Tr(x)$ by the stated dot schedule and return stationary before the solve only with the supplied certificate that this exact gradient is zero; if evaluating the product fails, return gradient-evaluation-failure; if the computed product is a rounded zero without that certificate, return gradient-unverified and do not form a ratio. Otherwise perform the augmented construction and linear solve afresh inside this attempt at its current damping: Form $A_\lambda=[J(x);\sqrt\lambda D]$ and $b_\lambda=[r(x);0]$, then call [[alg-gauss-newton-qr-svd-step-with-rank-safeguard]] in QR mode on $(A_\lambda,b_\lambda)$. Exact mode uses the exact positive square root and requires a supplied exact reduced factorization of $A_\lambda$ for each call; absence of that factorization returns linear-solve-failure. This matrix has full column rank because $D$ is nonsingular and $\lambda>0$. In computed mode, copy the stored $J(x)$ and $r(x)$ into the top blocks, compute $t=\operatorname{fl}(\sqrt\lambda)$, then fill the bottom block entries $\operatorname{fl}(tD_{ij})$ in increasing row and column order and fill the appended residual entries with exact zeros. Any first arithmetic or range failure in this construction returns linear-solve-failure with its stage and indices. The call receives a computed QR report for this actual stored $A_\lambda$. A computed-candidate is usable only when that report includes the low-level procedure's independently verified full-rank certificate $s_\lambda>0$ for the actual stored matrix, namely $\|A_\lambda v\|_2\ge s_\lambda\|v\|_2$ for every $v\in\mathbb R^n$. Pass this bound as the computed report's certificate field; it is not inferred from a nonzero computed diagonal or from positive definiteness of the ideal exact system alone. A rank-unverified report and every other status besides exact-step in exact mode or computed-candidate in computed mode are unusable and return linear-solve-failure with the report. A computed-candidate remains a candidate and carries no convergence guarantee. If the solver status is not exact-step in exact mode or computed-candidate in computed mode, return linear-solve-failure with its report; in particular, rank-unverified is a failure, not a usable trial. 2. If exact mode returns $p=0$ after the nonzero-gradient check, return linear-solve-failure with the inconsistent exact solve report. If computed mode returns $p=0$, return zero-step-unverified and do not compute a ratio. For every remaining candidate $p$ (the zero candidates have already returned a status), compute $\operatorname{pred}=m_0(0)-m_0(p)$. If this computation fails, return model-evaluation-failure; if $\operatorname{pred}\le0$, return nonpositive-predicted-decrease. In either case do not compute a ratio. 3. If $x+p\notin U$ or $\|Dp\|_2>\Delta$, reject the trial and compute the damping update $\lambda^+=\gamma\lambda$ in the selected arithmetic. If that update fails, is nonfinite, or is outside the representable range, return damping-range-failure with the current $x,\lambda$ and the trial report. Otherwise set $\lambda\leftarrow\lambda^+$ and continue. 4. Otherwise evaluate $r(x+p)$ and compute $\operatorname{ared}=\phi(x)-\phi(x+p)$ and $\rho=\operatorname{ared}/\operatorname{pred}$. A failed trial evaluation or nonfinite computed result returns trial-evaluation-failure. If $\rho<\eta_1$, reject and compute $\lambda^+=\gamma\lambda$ in the selected arithmetic. If that damping update fails, is nonfinite, or is outside the representable range, return damping-range-failure with the current $x,\lambda$ and the trial report. Otherwise set $\lambda\leftarrow\lambda^+$. If this was attempt $N$, return rejection-budget-exhausted; otherwise continue. 5. If $\rho\ge\eta_1$, first determine the next damping. Otherwise set $\lambda_{\rm next}=\max\{\lambda_{\min},q\}$. In every other accepted case set $\lambda_{\rm next}=\lambda$.
